title: Cloud platform/infrastructure scope reduction
transcript:
Platform Engineering Lead: Alright team, let's discuss our cloud provider options for the Q1 2023 MVP launch. We've been considering Google Cloud Platform, Azure, and building an on-premises data center.

SRE: I've been looking at the numbers, and AWS seems to be the most cost-effective solution for our use case. Google Cloud is about 20% more expensive.

Finance Partner: That's a significant difference, especially considering our budget.

CTO: Agreed. Let's focus on AWS then. But remember, we shouldn't rule out potential benefits from other options entirely.

Platform Engineering Lead: I'd like to address the on-premises data center option. It requires a $3M initial investment and a 50% increase in operational costs. That's too much for the benefits it would provide.

SRE: I've also looked at Azure. While it could potentially reduce technical debt through better integration with the hospital group's existing Microsoft suite, there are concerns about the learning curve and associated training costs.

CTO: Valid points, but we should consider the potential for scalability and performance that Azure might offer.

Platform Engineering Lead: I'll look into Azure further to evaluate potential benefits and address the learning curve concern.

SRE: I'd like to add that an MVP allows us to launch with essential features, minimizing technical debt and accelerating time to market.

CTO: Well said, SRE. That's a compelling reason to focus on AWS for our MVP.

Finance Partner: With the Q1 2023 deadline approaching, we need a platform that is already well-established and widely adopted, such as AWS.

CTO: I agree. Let's move forward with transitioning to AWS as our cloud provider and prioritize the MVP for our Q1 2023 launch.

Platform Engineering Lead: Understood. I'll begin the transition process and start planning for the MVP development.

(Off-topic exchange)

SRE: By the way, how's the company softball game coming along?

Finance Partner: Oh, it's a mess. No one can agree on a day that works for everyone.

SRE: Classic organizational chaos. Maybe we should leave it to the platform, after all.

CTO: (Laughs) Agreed, let's focus on our priorities first. AWS transition and MVP launch.

CTO: Alright, I'm signing off on this decision. Platform Engineering Lead, you will own it.

Platform Engineering Lead: Understood. I'll keep you all updated on our progress.

(Meeting adjourned)

Title: Cloud Migration Decision - AWS Transition for Q1 2023 MVP Launch

Record: The team has decided to transition to Amazon Web Services (AWS) as the cloud provider, prioritizing the launch of a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) in Q1 2023. This decision follows a preliminary assessment of AWS migration costs, which may include potential savings from reduced technical debt. The CTO will oversee this transition. Further evaluation of potential benefits from other platforms, such as Azure, will be undertaken by the Platform Engineering Lead to address any learning curve concerns. The MVP approach will minimize technical debt and accelerate time to market.
